Result of Service
Deliverable 1 – Course design documents: Course design documents for both new courses, setting out the target audience and entry requirements, learning outcomes, course topics, session structure and timings against the 40 hours, the practical/theoretical balance, the exercise and assessment approach, and the source material to be relied on. To be cleared by the Programme before full development begins. Due by 19 December 2026. Deliverable 2 – Draft curricula for peer review: Draft curricula and lesson plans for both new courses, in a form suitable for technical peer review by the Programme’s specialist consultant. Due by 15 January 2027. Deliverable 3 – Two complete course packages: Final, complete 40-hour course packages for (i) the management of a counter-terrorism or serious crime investigation and (ii) leading a kidnap investigation, each containing the full set of materials listed under Duties and Responsibilities, revised to address peer review and Programme feedback. Due by 13 February 2027. Deliverable 4 – Three tailored course packages: Revised versions of the Ethical Decision-Making; Briefing, Debriefing and Report Writing; and Ethical Questioning and Elicitation Techniques courses, tailored for kidnap, hostage-taking and extortion investigations, each accompanied by a short note recording what was changed and why. Due by 28 February 2027. Deliverable 5 – Handover: Handover to UNOCT of all materials, source files and supporting references developed or adapted under this assignment, indexed for inclusion in UNOCT’s digital repository, together with a short closing note identifying any recommended further development. Due by 28 February 2027
Work Location
Home Based
Expected duration
3 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The Individual Contractor will work under the overall supervision of the Officer-in-Charge or Programme Manager and the direct supervision of the Programme Management Officer responsible for the Global Programme on Counter-Terrorism Investigations. The Individual Contractor will be tasked with: • Designing and developing a new advanced-level course of 40 hours on the management of a counter-terrorism or serious crime investigation, covering the role and responsibilities of the investigation manager, investigative decision-making and record-keeping, initial response, crime scene management, core investigative strategies, the management of victims, witnesses and suspects, media and communications, and the management of the investigation to conclusion. • Designing and developing a new advanced-level course of 40 hours on leading a kidnap investigation, covering the threat and typologies, the objectives and responsibilities of the lead investigator, initial response and reporting, the mobilization and coordination of resources, operational functions and their interfaces (command, negotiation and covert functions), decision-making, communications with the media and with victims’ families, resolution planning, recovery and apprehension, and post-incident management and victim care. • Reviewing and as required, tailoring three existing Programme courses — Ethical Decision-Making; Briefing, Debriefing and Report Writing; and Ethical Questioning and Elicitation Techniques — so that their content, scenarios and assessment are fit for use in the context of kidnap, hostage-taking and extortion investigations. • Developing, for each new and tailored course, the full course package required by the Programme, including the course information sheet and learning outcomes, the lesson plan with timings, the trainer narrative, the participant study guide, the exercise book with scenarios and facilitator notes, the presentation materials, and the knowledge checks and assessment instruments. • Ensuring that the two new courses and the three tailored courses are coherent with one another and with the Programme’s wider training offer, with no unintended duplication and with a clear progression between levels. • Submitting draft curricula of the two new courses for technical peer review by a specialist consultant engaged separately by the Programme and addressing the review findings in the final versions. • Participating in design, review and clearance meetings with the Programme team by video conference and responding to consolidated feedback from the Programme and its expert reviewers. All course materials must be developed to the Programme’s course design standard, in English, and must be capable of being contextualized to different national legal and operational settings and translated into French. All materials must integrate international human rights standards, including gender-sensitive and trauma-informed practice, and must be consistent with the United Nations Manual of Guidance for Countering Kidnapping and Extortion and the UN Manual on Investigative Interviewing where relevant. All material gathered, developed, reviewed or adapted by the Individual Contractor under this assignment is the property of the United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism. All such material, together with source files, must be handed over to UNOCT before the contract terminates, for inclusion in UNOCT’s digital repository
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in law, criminology, policing, education, social sciences or a related field is required. A first level university degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in a similar field in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. A recognized senior investigating officer, investigation manager or equivalent command-level law enforcement qualification, combined with the experience set out below, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. • A minimum of 10 (ten) years of progressively responsible professional experience in law enforcement, including the management, command or leadership of serious and complex criminal or counter-terrorism investigations, is required. • Demonstrable experience of managing or leading investigations into crimes in action, including kidnapping, hostage-taking or extortion, in the role of investigation manager, senior investigating officer, lead investigator or equivalent, is required • Demonstrable experience in the design and development of law enforcement training curricula at management or command level, including lesson plans, trainer narrative, scenario-based exercises and assessment instruments, is required. Candidates will be asked to provide a sample of curriculum material they have authored • Experience of operating within, or advising, a command structure during a live incident involving a threat to life is required. • Experience in the development of law enforcement standard operating procedures, doctrine or accredited curricula is desirable. • Familiarity with the United Nations Manual of Guidance for Countering Kidnapping and Extortion is desirable. • Experience of designing training intended for contextualization to different national legal and operational settings, and for translation, is desirable. • Experience in human rights-based approaches and gender-sensitive and trauma-informed practice in investigations, and an understanding of the ethical issues arising in investigations involving victims of kidnapping, is desirable. • Knowledge and experience of the UN System and in particular of UNOCT is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For the post advertised, fluency in English is required, and all materials are to be developed in English. Knowledge of French is desirable, as the materials will subsequently be translated for francophone beneficiaries. Knowledge of another official United Nations language is an advantage.
Additional Information
Not available.
No Fee
THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.
